requirement: The `habeas` skill's reference on distributed requirements MUST give the guidance of {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.when`, {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.queries`, {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.site_text`, and {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.reviews` as a list of things to do and a list of things not to do.
rationale:
structural: The only structural obligation in `requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.lists` is the form of the guidance. Clause: "MUST give the guidance of … when, … queries, … site_text, and … reviews as a list of things to do and a list of things not to do." An alternative that gave the same advice as prose paragraphs, or as one mixed list, would keep the same information but break this clause. So the clause is a real structural obligation, and the root `assets/skills/habeas/references/distributed-requirements.md` meets it.

The file has a `## Do` section (`section[Distributed requirements]/section[Do]`) and a `## Don't` section (`section[Distributed requirements]/section[Don't]`). Each is a bulleted list.

The four pieces of guidance are spread across those two lists:
- **`when`:** the first Do bullet says to make a requirement distributed only when its obligation applies on its own at each site, and to use `{impl}` where particular code carries it out as a whole. The third Do bullet says to separate the obligations each site upholds from those particular code carries out, and to mark that code `{impl}`.
- **`queries`:** the Do bullets tell the agent to give every query `match` and `no_match` snippets, and to write a violation query for every construct that could break the obligation. They also tell it to check that the site queries select every place the obligation applies and no others.
- **`site_text`:** the Do bullet says to describe sites exactly as the queries select them and to state conventions as obligations. The Don't bullets say not to describe sites more broadly than the queries select, and not to state per-site obligations a reviewer cannot check from the site and its helpers.
- **`reviews`:** the Don't bullet says not to reference the distributed requirement from a site just because it is a site. The Do bullet says to let `habeas author --all` author the site reviews. The Don't bullet says not to re-run a false site review, and to fix the site or tighten the queries or text instead.

The Queries, Gotchas and Review sections add context and do not change that the guidance is given as Do and Don't lists. How well each piece of guidance matches its own requirement is a content question for those requirements. It is not a structural obligation of `lists`. No missing root or gap was found, and no acknowledgments apply.

behavioral: **Obligation.** `requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.lists` requires the `habeas` skill's distributed-requirements reference to give the guidance of `when`, `queries`, `site_text` and `reviews` as a list of things to do and a list of things not to do. The cited requirements are context. What each one says is assessed in its own tests.

**Test.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_give_distributed_guidance_as_do_and_dont_lists]` reads the real reference through `distributed_reference()`. That is `assets/skills/habeas/references/distributed-requirements.md`.
- **List form.** It splits out the `## Do` and `## Don't` sections and collects the top-level `- ` bullets of each. Each section must have at least two bullets. Every `## Do` bullet must not start with `- Don't `. Every `## Don't` bullet must start with `- Don't `. A missing heading, a prose-only section, or a mixed-up list would fail.
- **Guidance inside the lists.** `assert_text` is run on `section(.., "## Do")` and `section(.., "## Don't")`. The `section` helper stops at the next heading of the same or a higher level outside code fences, so the phrases must sit inside those lists.
  - `when`: "Make a requirement distributed only when" and "Separate obligations each site upholds".
  - `queries`: "Write a violation query", "Give every query `match` and `no_match` snippets", and the check that the site queries select every place the obligation applies and no others.
  - `site_text`: "Describe sites exactly as the site queries select them" in Do, and "Don't describe sites more broadly" and "Don't state a per-site obligation" in Don't.
  - `reviews`: "Let `habeas author --all` author the site reviews." in Do, and "Don't reference the distributed requirement from a site" and "Don't re-run a false site review for a different result" in Don't.

**Gaps considered.** The requirement does not say each topic must appear in both lists, so the absence of `when` and `queries` items in Don't is not a gap. I read the `## Don't` section and it matches the asserted bullets. Whether each bullet fully carries its own requirement, such as the "use `{impl}` instead" detail, belongs to the tests of the cited requirements. Behavior that would violate this requirement is guidance placed outside the lists, or lists in the wrong form. The structural loop and the phrase checks would catch both. The test carries the `{test}` reference to the subject, so there is no marking gap.

text: The `habeas` skill's reference on distributed requirements MUST give the guidance of {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.when`, {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.queries`, {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.site_text`, and {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.reviews` as a list of things to do and a list of things not to do.

The bundled skills MUST direct agents to make a requirement distributed only when its obligation applies on its own at each of many sites, such as a convention every validation function follows; to use `{impl}` instead when particular code carries out the requirement as a whole; and to mark with `{impl}` the code that carries out any obligation of a distributed requirement that its sites do not uphold.

The bundled skills MUST direct agents to write site queries that select every place the obligation applies and no others, violation queries for every kind of construct that could break it, and, for every query, `match` and `no_match` snippets that test its conditions.

The bundled skills MUST direct agents to describe sites exactly as the site queries select them, to state as an obligation any convention the queries rely on, such as how a list is named, and to state only per-site obligations that a reviewer can check from the site and the helpers it calls.

The bundled skills MUST tell agents that sites need no reference to the requirement, that `habeas author --all` authors site reviews under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, and that a false site review is addressed by fixing the site, or by tightening the queries or the requirement text when the site should not be covered or the text admits more than one reading, under {cite}`requirements.cli.flip_guidance`, not by re-running the review.
